Draft a deterministic proof for the claim below using ONLY the six tools. Each tool call counts toward a 12-call budget; plan for at most lookup_source, get_premise, verify_derivation and propose_finding. Do NOT call list_dependent_claims or request_lawyer_review — they belong to other tasks and only waste your budget. Always call lookup_source for the cited source before proposing, and always call verify_derivation on the exact proof object before propose_finding — propose only a proof the checker accepted. Cite only admitted premises (lawyer_confirmed or document_extracted). Quote provision and clause text verbatim. When the checker rejects a draft, fix the flagged steps and retry. End with propose_finding carrying the full proof object.

Session matter: MAT-01. Use the ids below EXACTLY as written — never invent, shorten or reformat an id.

Claim: Does clause 9.2 require Nimbus to keep transfer logs?
Claim type: CT2 params: {'element': 'transfer logs'}
As of: 2026-11-20

Target clause 9.2 Cross-border transfer for fraud screening:
Nimbus may transfer order data to its analytics cluster outside India for fraud screening. Such transfers are limited to order identifiers and risk scores, and Nimbus shall keep transfer logs for review.

Clause inventory (ref + heading):
1 Parties
2 Definitions
3 Scope of processing
4 Purpose limitation
5 Data categories
6 Security safeguards
7 Processor engagement
8 Sub-processors
9.1 Cross-border transfers, general
9.2 Cross-border transfer for fraud screening
10 Breach intimation
11 Retention and erasure

Sources (id | key | title):
SRC-DECOY | emblems-act-1950 | The Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950
SRC-DPDP-ACT | dpdp-act-2023 | The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
SRC-DPDP-RULES | dpdp-rules-2025 | The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
SRC-GSR-843E | commencement-gsr-843e-2025 | Commencement Notification G.S.R. 843(E)

Admitted premises (id | trust class | clause | statement):
F-LOOP-92 | document_extracted | CL-10 | Clause 9.2 requires Nimbus to keep transfer logs for review.

The proof object has exactly these fields: claim_id, as_of (YYYY-MM-DD, copy from "As of" above), conclusion ("holds" or "does not hold"), premises (list of {fact_id, statement, trust_class} copied verbatim from the admitted premises above), steps (list of step objects, the last one a conclude step). Step kinds and their fields: cite_fact {fact_id}; cite_rule {rule_card_id, citation {source_version_id, provision_id, span [start, end], sha256}} where the citation copies one provision from a lookup_source result (span [0, len(text)] of that provision, sha256 as returned); in_force {provision_id}; compare {value (number), op (one of <=, >=, ==, <, >), bound (number)}; contains_element {clause_id, quote} where quote is a verbatim substring of the target clause text above; role_applies {party, role, clause_id, quote} with the same verbatim quote rule; conclude {conclusion} repeating the proof conclusion. Prefer the smallest proof the checker accepts. The moment verify_derivation returns valid true, call propose_finding in the very next turn with the byte-identical proof object.

{"source_version_id": "SV-DPDP-ACT-V2SIM", "version_label": "v2-simulated", "effective_from": "2025-11-13", "effective_until": null, "is_simulated": true, "provisions": [{"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s1-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s1", "text": "1. Short title and commencement.

(1) This Act may be called the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.
", "sha256": "c1a9c0242d430e3448383381b6a967a54b4d690a1ebedb78ca10ee830c841e26"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s8-1-2-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s8(1)-(2)", "text": "8. General obligations of Data Fiduciary.

(1) A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or failure of a Data Principal to carry out the duties provided under this Act, be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.

(2) A Data Fiduciary may engage, appoint, use or otherwise involve a Data Processor to process personal data on its behalf for any activity related to offering of goods or services to Data Principals only under a valid contract.
", "sha256": "8208fc4d0cb31f9b0b03c3045390c40f477c6d70e30626199b53822c55a45b0d"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s8-4-5-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s8(4)-(5)", "text": "(4) A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

(5) A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach.
", "sha256": "ab78aaa47226004d0707937c722b7e7147fa6784ce750a52e6b22a25db8411b1"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s8-6-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s8(6)", "text": "(6) In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach in such form and manner as may be prescribed:

Provided that [SIMULATED AMENDMENT v2 — not part of the enacted Act] intimation to the Board under this sub-section shall be given within forty-eight hours of the Data Fiduciary becoming aware of the breach.
", "sha256": "7459d6ba1ccee7925f84b09aee06f92e96493b874bc5bdbc6807bb454c4ca066"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s8-7-8-s12-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s8(7)-(8)_s12", "text": "(7) A Data Fiduciary shall, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law for the time being in force,—

(a) erase personal data, upon the Data Principal withdrawing her consent or as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the specified purpose is no longer being served, whichever is earlier; and

(b) cause its Data Processor to erase any personal data that was made available by the Data Fiduciary for processing to such Data Processor.

Illustrations.

(I) X, an individual, registers herself on an online marketplace operated by Y, an e-commerce service provider. X gives her consent to Y for the processing of her personal data for selling her used car. The online marketplace helps conclude the sale. Y shall no longer retain her personal data.

(II) X, an individual, decides to close her savings account with Y, a bank. Y is required by law applicable to banks to maintain the record of the identity of its clients for a period of ten years beyond closing of accounts. Since retention is necessary for compliance with law, Y shall retain X's personal data for the said period.

(8) The purpose referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (7) shall be deemed to no longer be served, if the Data Principal does not––

(a) approach the Data Fiduciary for the performance of the specified purpose; and

(b) exercise any of her rights in relation to such processing,

for such time period as may be prescribed, and different time periods may be prescribed for different classes of Data Fiduciaries and for different purposes.

(11) For the purposes of this section, it is hereby clarified that a Data Principal shall be considered as not having approached the Data Fiduciary for the performance of the specified purpose, in any period during which she has not initiated contact with the Data Fiduciary for such performance, in person or by way of communication in electronic or physical form.

12. Right to correction and erasure of personal data.

(1) A Data Principal shall have the right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of her personal data for the processing of which she has previously given consent, including consent as referred to in clause (a) of section 7, in accordance with any requirement or procedure under any law for the time being in force.

(2) A Data Fiduciary shall, upon receiving a request for correction, completion or updating from a Data Principal,—

(a) correct the inaccurate or misleading personal data;

(b) complete the incomplete personal data; and

(c) update the personal data.

(3) A Data Principal shall make a request in such manner as may be prescribed to the Data Fiduciary for erasure of her personal data, and upon receipt of such a request, the Data Fiduciary shall erase her personal data unless retention of the same is necessary for the specified purpose or for compliance with any law for the time being in force.
", "sha256": "72d99b5ef7c9cb870d67fb1a53bfc130ba9ab059ba493572dab1896e9c34d229"}], "truncated": false}
